description: Reviews netdoctor, a network health-check CLI that writes nothing locally. Every run sends DNS queries, an ICMP ping, a TCP connect, HTTP GET requests, and usually a traceroute to hosts and paths taken from its arguments, so the arguments can carry data out. Live --watch and --mtr monitors repeat those probes until interrupted and are reviewed separately.
name: netdoctor network diagnostics
saferAlternatives: Check that every target host, URL, and --path value is one you mean to contact and carries no secrets, since netdoctor sends them out in DNS queries and HTTP requests.
Run a one-shot check (netdoctor <host>) or pass --json, which runs the ladder once even with --watch or --mtr.
If a live monitor is needed, add --max-runs N so it stops on its own instead of probing until interrupted.
